patch_description:
The existing program was broken in many ways: `column_recursion` wrote rows via `result_df.loc[i] = ...` into an empty DataFrame (misaligned/mislabeled results), reordered *cell values* rather than per-row column permutations (violating the API which must return per-row column orderings), dropped the returned `column_orderings` (always `[]`), contained column-name mutation bugs, and used adjacency/squared-length heuristics that don't match the actual character-Trie prefix objective.

I rewrote the editable algorithm to directly target the real objective:
- Serialize each cell once (empty string for NaN) and factorize values to integer codes.
- Build up to three bounded whole-dataset candidate per-row column orderings:
  1) A global frequency ordering ranked by `sum(len(v)*count(v)*(count(v)-1))` per column with deterministic tie breaks;
  2) A recursive conditional prefix partition tree on integer codes, splitting groups on the field with the best length-weighted repetition, tail-ordered deterministically;
  3) A variant with a different length/frequency tradeoff.
- Score each candidate exactly with the ideal Trie objective: sum of adjacent LCPs after sorting the serialized row strings (binary-search LCP with C-speed slice comparisons).
- Return the best candidate's DataFrame (object dtype, identical values) plus valid per-row column orderings (list of column names per row), preserving shape, row identity, all cell values, and honoring `col_merge`/`one_way_dep`/stops. Runtime is bounded via depth caps, candidate column limits, and shared precomputation.
